summary: The A Stronger Workforce for America Act of 2026 reauthorizes and updates the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act (WIOA). The legislation sets funding levels for various workforce development programs, transfers adult education and family literacy functions to the Department of Labor, modifies state and local workforce boards and plans, changes performance accountability metrics, revises the training provider eligibility process, introduces new grant programs, and establishes pilot projects.

affected_groups.effect: Gain expanded access to training programs, work-based learning, individual training accounts, and support services, with specific funding prioritizations for low-income individuals, public assistance recipients, and dislocated workers.
Subject to updated eligibility rules, increased out-of-school youth funding priority percentages, and new opportunities through youth apprenticeship and reentry programs.
Engage more directly in skills development programs, employer-directed training agreements, and sector partnerships, with cost-sharing requirements based on employer size.
Must meet revised performance criteria for credential attainment and job placement to remain on eligible provider lists, while becoming eligible for new grant funding opportunities.
Required to review regional and local area alignments, update plans, manage performance accountability measures, and oversee new funding allocations and local boards.

key_provisions: Reauthorizes appropriations for youth workforce investment activities, adult employment and training activities, and dislocated worker employment and training activities through fiscal year 2032.
Transfers all functions of the Adult Education and Family Literacy Act from the Department of Education to the Department of Labor.
Modifies performance accountability indicators for states and local areas, emphasizing employment outcomes, credential attainment, and work-based learning participation.
Revises eligibility criteria and performance requirements for training service providers, introducing tiers such as Workforce Innovation Leader designations and employer-sponsored programs.

Authorizes new competitive grant programs, including the Youth Apprenticeship Readiness Grant Program, Strengthening Community Colleges Workforce Development Grants Program, Reentry Employment Opportunities Program, and 'Make America Skilled Again' consolidated pilot grants.
Updates the Job Corps program by changing 'centers' to 'campuses,' expanding eligibility rules, strengthening campus safety standards, and revising performance improvement and closure processes.
Establishes a Center for Technical Assistance for Transforming to Competitive Integrated Employment through the Department of Labor in partnership with other federal agencies.
missing_information: Exact overall budgetary impacts beyond the specific program authorization amounts listed for fiscal years 2027 through 2032.
Specific local economic data for every individual state and workforce development area that may influence future board realignments or performance thresholds.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The A Stronger Workforce for America Act of 2026 reauthorizes and updates the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act (WIOA). The legislation sets funding levels for various workforce development programs, transfers adult education and family literacy functions to the Department of Labor, modifies state and local workforce boards and plans, changes performance accountability metrics, revises the training provider eligibility process, introduces new grant programs, and establishes pilot projects.
summary_detail.significance: The legislation significantly alters the structure, oversight, and administration of federal workforce development, adult education, and job training programs. By shifting adult education functions to the Department of Labor, tightening performance metrics for training providers, expanding employer-driven training models, and authorizing broad pilot projects, the bill aims to realign federal workforce investments with contemporary economic and industrial demands. The legislation authorizes multi-billion dollar funding levels across numerous programs through fiscal year 2032, impacting state and local agencies, educational institutions, training providers, and program participants nationwide.
